raw_response:
I will keep my plan simple and put most of my land into spring maize, because that fits my usual way of farming in Quzhou County, matches my well irrigation, and gives me a stable main crop. I will keep a smaller area in stevia for cash income, but not too much, because it needs closer management and more labor. With 57 mu and a 4-person household, I want a plan I can finish on time without stretching labor too much. For maize, I will use hybrid seed because I want stronger stand and better yield, and I will use moderate fertilizer with a few irrigations from the well to protect the crop if spring or early summer is dry. I will use rotary tillage because it is practical and fast for me at the start of the season. For stevia, I will also use improved planting material, but I will give it a bit more potassium and more pest control than maize because leaf quality matters. I will not over-irrigate, but I will water enough to keep growth steady. Overall, I will aim for a balanced year: maize for dependable production, stevia for added income, and input levels that I can afford and manage.
